claims.text: A single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti high-entropy alloy has coercivity below 100 Oe.
Chemical disorder and high configurational entropy suppress orbital moments and stabilize a paramagnetic or weakly ferromagnetic state in fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti.
Aging or controlled annealing can produce an L12-ordered secondary phase within an fcc high-entropy-alloy matrix.
The proposed L12 precipitates can specifically be Co3Ti or Fe3Ti in an Fe-Co-Ni-Ti matrix.
The Ti- and Co-rich L12 precipitates will be ferromagnetic.
The L12 precipitates will retain both structural and ferromagnetic order between 300 K and 600 K.
An fcc matrix containing L12 precipitates can possess a thermally stable high-temperature microstructure.
L12 strengthening precipitates can have high anti-phase-boundary energy.
Interfaces between the fcc matrix and L12 precipitates act as magnetic-domain-wall pinning centers.
Chemical ordering in the L12 precipitates enhances orbital-moment contributions relative to the disordered fcc matrix.
Introducing a second ordered phase creates local variations in exchange interactions and magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Anti-phase-boundary energy and precipitate-interface strain fields provide strong magnetic-domain-wall pinning.
Domain-wall pinning increases the energy barrier for magnetic reversal and thereby raises coercivity.
L12 precipitation stabilizes a non-collinear magnetic ground state in Fe-Co-Ni-Ti.
A dual-phase fcc plus L12 Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy will exhibit coercivity exceeding 100 Oe above room temperature.
The dual-phase alloy will show a distinct hysteresis-loop shape diagnostic of strong pinning.
Coherent or semi-coherent precipitate interfaces are required for the proposed coercivity enhancement.
Decomposition into BCC or B2 phases would dilute the magnetic moment or reduce pinning efficiency.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis specifies Ti- and Co-rich L12 precipitates, but Fe3Ti is offered as an example even though that nominal compound contains no Co.
The operating regime is described as significantly or well above room temperature, yet 300 K—approximately room temperature—is included as a representative operating and test temperature.
